subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Amplitude and Decibels
description: A quick, practical guide to Amplitude and Decibels.

hook.text: A jet engine is a million times louder than a whisper. Decibels compress that range.

buildup.text: Decibels use a logarithmic scale. Every 10 dB increase means ten times more power.

discovery.text: 0 dB is the threshold of hearing. 120 dB is the threshold of pain. A compact range.

twist.text: Negative decibels mean attenuation — a -3 dB filter cuts power in half.

climax.text: Audio engineers, RF designers, and acousticians all think in decibels daily.

punchline.text: A million-to-one ratio becomes 60 dB. Logs tame enormous ranges.

quiz.question: What does a -3 dB change represent in terms of power?
